assumptions.text: Depth light and scale 1-3 deployables / 1 team come from the brief (two part-time developers); nothing suggests more.
Concession approval is a volunteer judgement on uploaded proof, not an automated check.
Cash taken at the desk is recorded in the system by the volunteer; the cash tin itself is out of scope.
Members are households, but the member number and borrowing limits attach to one named person.
About 400 members and 600 items over the first year (order of magnitude from a typical UK tool library).

open_questions.text: Does a lapsed membership block returns and fee payment, or only new borrowing?
Is the 48-hour reservation hold counted in calendar hours or only over desk opening days?
Who decides that damage exceeds fair wear and sets the charge - the desk volunteer or the coordinator?

notes_for_downstream.text: 'Tool' means a catalogue entry (a kind of thing, e.g. 'cordless drill') to members browsing, but a specific asset-tagged item to volunteers at the desk and in maintenance. Keep 'tool' and 'item' apart; it is a boundary between catalogue and lending/maintenance.

Borrowing eligibility is a cross-cutting rule: membership current, fee balance zero, no overdue item, fewer than three items out. Which context owns the decision is a real design call - do not let three contexts each half-own it.
Card payments go through Stripe and card data never touches the system (constraint C1). Do not build payment processing; wrap the provider.
Late fees accrue daily (GBP 1 per item per day, capped at replacement value) - accrual is time-driven, not user-driven, so something must run on a clock.

system.name: Toolshare
system.one_liner: A neighbourhood library where residents pay a small yearly fee and borrow tools instead of buying them.
system.problem: Members cannot tell whether a tool is in without phoning; volunteers lose track of who has what and forget to log returns; late fees go uncollected, so tools come back late and the library loses money.
system.why_now: The library has outgrown a spreadsheet, a paper sign-out book and a cash tin; membership is growing and the volunteers are burning out on admin.

customer_segments: Local households that need a tool occasionally
value_propositions: Borrow the tool you need for a fortnight for a fraction of its price
Know before you leave home whether a tool is in and reserve it
customer_relationships: Self-service online, volunteer-assisted at the desk

value_proposition_links.value_proposition: Borrow the tool you need for a fortnight for a fraction of its price
Know before you leave home whether a tool is in and reserve it

goals.metric: share of loans returned by the due date
share of late and damage fees paid within 30 days of being charged

actors.name: Member
actors.description: A resident household that pays the annual fee and borrows tools.

actors.name: Desk volunteer
actors.description: Runs the Saturday desk: checks tools out and in, takes cash, notes condition.

actors.name: Maintenance volunteer
actors.description: Inspects, repairs and retires tools; adds donated tools.

actors.name: Coordinator
actors.description: Part-time staff member: approves concessions, waives fees, sets damage charges.

actors.name: Stripe
actors.description: Card payment provider; holds card data on our behalf.

impacts.change: Returns the tool by the due date because a reminder arrives two days before
Pays a late fee online the week it is charged instead of waiting for the next desk visit
Records every return at the moment it happens, with condition, in under five minutes

deliverables.description: Due-date reminder by email two days before and on the day
One seven-day renewal a member can do online when nobody has reserved the item
Pay-a-fee link in the late notice that charges the card
Desk return screen: scan the asset tag, tick condition, done

capabilities.name: Membership
capabilities.description: Joining, annual renewal, concession approval, lapsing, member standing.

capabilities.name: Tool catalogue
capabilities.description: What tools exist as kinds, their replacement value, safety notes and induction needs, and which physical items belong to each.

capabilities.name: Lending
capabilities.description: Reserving, checking out, renewing and returning items within the 14-day, three-items, no-overdue rules.

capabilities.name: Fees
capabilities.description: Daily late-fee accrual capped at replacement value, damage charges, waivers, and a member's balance.

capabilities.name: Card payments
capabilities.description: Taking a card payment for a fee or membership through a provider.

capabilities.name: Tool maintenance
capabilities.description: Inspections, repairs, condition tracking and retirement of physical items.

constraints.text: PCI: card data never touches the library's systems; cards are handled by Stripe end to end.
Two part-time developers and no on-call; anything that needs babysitting will not be run.
One Postgres database and a small web application are the agreed shape; no additional infrastructure budget.
UK GDPR: member contact details and proof of concession are personal data with a retention limit.

non_goals: Inter-library transfers or a network of libraries

existing_systems.name: Shared spreadsheet and paper sign-out book
existing_systems.role: Today's record of members, tools and loans

alternatives.name: Shared spreadsheet plus paper sign-out book
alternatives.strengths: Free, everyone understands it, no training
alternatives.weaknesses: Nobody knows what is out, returns go unlogged, fees are never chased

alternatives.name: Phoning the desk to ask if a tool is in
alternatives.strengths: Personal, works for people without internet
alternatives.weaknesses: Only works on Saturday mornings; no reservation, so the tool may be gone on arrival

alternatives.name: Buying or hiring the tool
alternatives.strengths: Immediate, keep it as long as you like
alternatives.weaknesses: Expensive for a one-off job; storage; waste

alternatives.name: myTurn (hosted lending-library software)
alternatives.strengths: Runs many tool libraries today; membership, catalogue and card payments out of the box
alternatives.weaknesses: Per-member pricing; generic loan rules; cannot express this library's fee cap, concession approval or desk workflow without workarounds

scale_target.users: hundreds of members, about twenty volunteers
scale_target.notes: one team of two part-time devs, modular monolith preferred, single Postgres

plain_words.what: We wrote down why the tool library needs a system, who uses it, what success looks like in numbers, and how big the build may get.
plain_words.decided: Two goals: 90% of loans back on time and 80% of fees paid within 30 days. One team, 1 to 3 deployable parts. Six capabilities; card payments are bought, not built.
plain_words.assumed: That the library's own lending and fee rules (14 days, three items, GBP 1 a day capped) are the thing worth building, and that a hosted product like myTurn cannot express them well enough.
plain_words.riskiest: If myTurn or similar fits after all, most of the custom build below is wasted and the library should have configured a product instead.
